exact_term_scan.note: A raw 'Jabor' hit was an unrelated 2012 news reference to Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabor Al Thani, not the 2018-2019 correspondent chain.

drone_uav_semantic_scan.result: The candidate set resolved to news/newsletters, military or policy material, consumer-drone mail, the 2014 Light & Strong solar-UAV investment lane, and the separate 2016 Levitection advanced-radar/security investment lane. Follow-up review of Levitection found concealed-weapons/near-field detection rather than counter-UAS technology. No personal raw-mail message identified the 2019 anti-drone supplier.

tested_leads.result: Real Barak-Epstein drone investment lane, but the technology is an unmanned aircraft platform, not counter-drone technology. No bridge to the 2019 Qatar anti-drone request was located.

tested_leads.result: Tested because radar is relevant to counter-UAS sensing. The located product and patent record concern near-field concealed-object/weapons detection, not aerial drone detection or defeat, and no document joins Levitection to Jabor's February 2019 anti-drone request.

tested_leads.result: Tested as a possible later counter-UAS bridge. No Barak/DOJ source located joins this contact to Barak's February 2019 anti-drone promise.

february_2019_jabor_index_reconciliation.result: Across the local Barak/DOJ forensic indexes, these were the only February 2019 Jabor-containing EFTA records located. They are the 'First of two emails' chain and its Carbyne/Lysys continuation; no second anti-drone email was located.

conclusion: The supplier behind Barak's 'still waiting for some information' remark remains unidentified. The negative finding is stronger after the NAS-wide audit, but it is not proof that the second email never existed: it may not have copied Epstein, may be outside the released corpus, or may survive in an unlocated later Barak mailbox export.
